items.title: Rapid-MLX 0.16.9: 47x faster first token on repeated long prompts (32K prompt 18.6 s to 0.39 s) and Flint 40B at 131 tok/s on a 36 GB Mac
items.summary: Rapid-MLX 0.16.9 for Apple Silicon reuses prompt state so a repeated ~32K-token prompt starts in 0.39 s instead of 18.6 s. Flint 40B (A2.5B, 4-bit) runs at 131 tok/s on a 36 GB Mac with tool calls and reasoning, parallel chats decode together for 2x aggregate throughput on Qwen3.8-27B, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B is added, and 'rapid-mlx launch codex' wires a coding agent to the local server. Numbers are the project's own.

items.title: Hermes Agent: new 'hermes record' plugin turns a recorded browser session into a reusable skill; MCP tools can now declare cost and per-chat spend limits
items.summary: Nous Research's Hermes Labs plugin workflow-record ('hermes plugins install workflow-record') records what you do in the browser, /learn turns the recording into a skill, and the agent replays it with new details. Separately, recent Hermes Agent PRs let an MCP server entry declare per-tool cost and a per-chat spend limit shown at approval time (#142470), surface MCP progress for long tool calls (#141985) and pick a separate subagent model (#141312).

items.title: LlamaIndex publishes a 37-page OCRia-1 technical report with evals against open-weight OCR models and full data/training pipeline details
items.summary: Follow-up to the OCRia-1 release (kept 2026-10-24): the report compares OCRia-1 with Infinity-Parser, LightOnOCR 3, Chandra 2 and dots.mocr on ParseBench, olmOCR-bench, PulseBench-Tab and fr-bench-pdf2md, claims 2x to 4x faster decoding than recent open-weight models, and includes 24 pages of appendix on data curation, training and eval findings.

items.title: NVIDIA AW-0 paper: one model generates skill code, predicts future video frames and outputs robot actions; 50.7% on RoboTwin 2.0 vs 41.3% for pi0.5
items.summary: 'Agentic World Action Models' (NVIDIA) generates reusable skill programs, future frames and actions together so code-based planning guides execution. Reported 50.7% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 vs 41.3% for pi0.5, and 71.1% vs 46.0% across eight real-world manipulation tasks. Paper-reported numbers.

saved_rejected.why: General security news (Tailscale Tailworm), not AI capability; forwarded as a security lead instead.

security_forwarded.matched: fleet tailnet (no Tailscale entry in stack.json); always_forward: containers/infra lateral movement
security_forwarded.note: Tailworm (Erica Windisch, Cyberdione Labs, published 2026-10-25): 11 unpatched findings tested on tailscale 1.104.2 and headscale 0.29.5. Tailscale SSH runs inside root tailscaled, so ssh -L/-R unix-socket forwarding reaches or replaces root-only sockets (lab: root, /etc/shadow, root RCE via a command daemon); path-check race; session-churn OOM; serve TCP forward to the localapi socket allows node takeover; conn25 app connector egress to any destination incl. cloud metadata; headscale unauthenticated memory/eviction and hostile-DERP 1.34 GB reads. Lab chain hopped device to device to root and enrolled a rogue node. No CVE, bulletin or fixed version yet; Tailscale has not confirmed. Interim: per-pair SSH grants (single src/dst), deny forwarding in SSH rules, 'tailscale set --ssh=false' where not needed (confirm other access first), drop unused app connector grants and serve forwards to unix sockets, enable node-key expiry, delete compromised nodes at the control plane. Also seen via @The_Cyber_News (2019 likes). Box: no tailscale/tailscaled/headscale binaries; fleet machines on the tailnet likely in scope.

security_forwarded.matched: Codex, Claude Code, Cursor CLI; always_forward: agent tooling
security_forwarded.note: Forever Security found a malicious AGENTS.md in a customer's ~/Downloads (the agent's working directory) that made a coding agent install the rogue npm package 'function-color'. A web page can silently drop AGENTS.md into Downloads in Chrome/Edge/Firefox. Repro: Codex ran the payload ~90% of the time; a malicious CLAUDE.md redirected Claude Code API traffic, exposed its OAuth token and got code exec ~50%. No vendor patch (intended behavior). Mitigation: never launch agents from ~/Downloads or home/broad dirs, review unfamiliar AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, keep approvals/sandbox on; fleet scheduled agents should pin cwd to project dirs. Box: no ~/Downloads, no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md under any Downloads path.

Two critical (CVSS 9.6) MCP Inspector advisories published 2026-10-21. GHSA-6x67-4w4w-9f3w: a remote MCP App in the Inspector sandbox (same origin as the proxy) steals the proxy auth token via inherited sessionStorage and calls /stdio for local RCE. GHSA-4fc4-wcmh-4g86: attacker OAuth callback injects params that switch transport from remote HTTP to local stdio and runs an attacker command on reconnect. Affected @modelcontextprotocol/inspector, inspector-client, inspector-server >=0.20.0 <=1.0.2; fixed 1.0.3 (v2 line: security release 2.12.0). Check for npx/global installs of the Inspector on fleet machines. Box: not installed (no global npm, no node_modules copy, no npx cache).

OpenCode Console (hosted gateway) breach of a legacy system the night of 2026-10-16/17: provider keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) saved in Console workspaces of 1.4% of users may be exposed and were used for unauthorized charges (hundreds to >$1,000). Open-source CLI/desktop not affected (local keys stay local). Affected users got an email 'Action Required: Potential provider key breach' on 2026-10-17. Action only if any fleet provider key was ever pasted into OpenCode Console: revoke at the provider, replace, review billing from 2026-10-16. Not previously logged by Magpie. Box: no opencode install or config.
